$schema.description: The JSON Schema this file follows, for editors.

bot.description: The bot settings file, relative to this file.

allowCommandCredentials.description: Whether a credential may come from a command, which then runs as the service; whoever can edit this file chooses that command.

issuer.description: The provider's issuer URL, where its OpenID configuration is discovered.

oneOf.description: A Secrets Manager secret's string, read with the process's own AWS credentials.

path.description: A file the platform mounts, such as a secret injector writes; read again as it rotates.

oneOf.description: A mounted file's contents, a trailing newline dropped.

command.description: The program and its arguments, run without a shell.

timeoutSeconds.description: How long the command may run before it is stopped.

oneOf.description: A command printing a Kubernetes ExecCredential (status.token, status.expirationTimestamp) on stdout, run again before the token expires; its stderr is discarded. Runs only under allowCommandCredentials.

tokenEndpoint.description: The identity provider's token endpoint, as its OpenID configuration names token_endpoint.

harnessAuth.description: How Chat authenticates to the Harness.

turnCredentials.description: How each Turn gets its User's AWS credentials.

oneOf.description: The Chat Service assumes the Memory role for each Turn with a session policy naming its User; no OIDC provider or session tags.
The Chat Service polls its own table and sends each due run to the run queue.
No scheduled tasks: the Chat Service offers none, and no queue, schedule group or scheduler grant is created.

liveView.description: How the User watches the Agent Computer's browser.

oneOf.description: The Agent Computer's browser streams its live view from AgentCore Browser to the User.
No live view: bot settings may not turn agentComputer.liveBrowser on, and the Chat Service is granted no live view stream.

network.description: A network that brings its own egress: BotCube creates, routes and parks no NAT in it, so the deploy identity names no aws.ecs.privateEgress.

privateSubnets.description: The services', browsers' and Lambdas' subnets, which must already reach the internet; the proxy carries only the services' own traffic.

sheet.description: Decrypts what the Sign-in Sheet encrypts: an RSA_2048 ENCRYPT_DECRYPT key.

streamArn.description: The table's NEW_IMAGE stream, which parking reads.

vault.description: The Credential Service's vault: partition key accountId, sort key provider.

connectionLogs.description: The origin load balancer's connection logs.

supplied.description: Resources the operator supplies, with their grants, instead of BotCube creating them: BotCube creates neither a supplied resource nor a policy on it, and `botcube footprint` lists the grants each one needs. Each one left out, BotCube creates and grants.

imageRegistry.description: The registry every image BotCube pulls comes from, a mirror of Amazon ECR Public's paths: the services' sidecars and every image BotCube builds FROM.

oneOf.description: AWS X-Ray, through each service's collector.

url.description: The OTLP/HTTP traces endpoint the services export to, such as http://collector:4318/v1/traces.

credential.description: Sent as `Authorization: Bearer <value>`; absent, exports are unauthenticated.
